questions.question: When a new tool like set_reminder is added to a project, what change is needed in the function that dispatches tool calls to their implementations?
options: An additional elif branch matching the new tool's name to its implementation
A brand new run_conversation function specific to that tool
Nothing — the API automatically routes calls to the right function
A change to the model parameter in the API request

questions.question: For Claude to be able to call a newly wired-in tool, what else has to happen besides implementing its function?
options: Its JSON schema must be added to the list of tools passed to Claude in run_conversation
The tool must be registered in a separate authentication step
The tool must be the only one in the tools list
The tool's schema must be sent as a system prompt instead of the tools parameter

questions.question: The course's approach sends every tool's full schema to Claude on every request. What's the main drawback of this pattern as opposed to a lookup-tool approach?
options: It's not the most efficient design — an alternative is exposing just tool names plus a lookup tool that fetches full schemas on demand
The API rejects requests with more than one tool schema
Claude cannot parse more than one schema per request
It requires a separate API key per tool

questions.question: Does the Claude API have a formal concept of dependency/ordering between multiple tool_use blocks returned in a single response?
options: No — the API has no such concept; Claude simply won't emit dependent calls together in the first place
Yes — each tool_use block includes a depends_on field
Yes — tool_use blocks are always executed in alphabetical order by tool name
Yes — the developer must specify ordering via the tool_choice parameter
